bull_bear.body:
- **₹25cr CCD raise, April 2026:** *"last month we raised approximately INR25 crores of equity through CCD,
  Compulsorily Convertible Debentures. This capital will be deployed towards scaling our secured MSME portfolios
  and supporting our digital lending initiatives."* Conversion terms, price and counterparty were **not disclosed**.
- **Capital is not the constraint; funding is.** CRAR 57.6% on ₹106cr net worth against ₹261cr AUM leaves
  substantial headroom — *"providing sufficient headroom for further growth"* — which is why the entire FY27 plan
  hinges on the ₹400–450cr lender pipeline rather than further equity.
- **Stated policy:** *"We also maintain conservative leverage and strong capital adequacy, which gives us the
  flexibility to grow in a calibrated manner."*
- **Liability strategy is to broaden and cheapen**: bank lines + venture debt + NCDs via wealth platforms today,
  PSU banks as the stated next unlock. **No dividend, buyback or promoter-holding discussion occurred on the call.**
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
1. **The call's own numbers do not reconcile.** Disbursement ₹142cr (prepared remarks) vs ₹147cr (Q&A); 90-day
   PAR ₹65–70 lakh vs ₹40–50–60 lakh; net NPA 0.74% vs 0.76% vs "0.75, 0.8"; cost of funds 13–14% vs "12 or 13";
   opex guidance 2.5–2.75% vs 2–2.5%; yield ~15% vs 20–24% lending ROIs. For a maiden call this is the single
   biggest watch-item — **re-verify every FY26 figure against the audited annual report before use.**
2. **Asset quality deteriorated and the driver is regional-political.** *"there was a Karja Mukti Abhiyan which
   happened in Punjab then Haryana. There were other issues which happened in Haryana, so there was a bit NPA
   that rose in our book as well."* Debt-waiver campaigns in the home geography are precisely the risk a
   400km-radius franchise cannot diversify away from.
3. **Concentration: geography + product + promoter.** North India only, one collateral type (constructed
   residential/commercial property), and a CFO who answered essentially every question on the call including all
   strategy — key-man exposure is visible in the transcript itself.
4. **The FY27 plan requires ₹400–450cr of new borrowing against a ₹261cr book.** If the lender pipeline slips,
   the ₹500–550cr AUM guide fails arithmetically; no contingency was described.
5. **Cost-of-funds guidance is aggressive and unbacked.** 13–14% → 11–12% *"Not more than 12 months"*, with PSU
   banks as the mechanism and **no PSU bank yet on the lender list.** Rating, if any, was never mentioned.
6. **The digital-lending leg is unproven at scale** — pilot-stage, salaried, ~24% flat / 6 months, and intended
   to be 15–20% of a doubled book within a year. *"There is no human intervention"* is a control claim, not an
   evidenced loss curve; no digital-book DPD was given separately.
7. **PPI licence is a NOC, not an approval** — the differentiation argument (§6a), the lead-generation engine
   (§6) and the QR collection rail (§7) all depend on it, and its own guided window has now lapsed.
8. **Legacy JLG run-off risk**: 10.5% of AUM with collections only and no new disbursement — recovery on a
   run-off MFI book in Punjab/Haryana is where the NPA already came from.
9. **Secured recovery is untested.** *"as of now, we are not in any recovery mode"* — only *"just one loan ticket
   size"* has gone to legal on the secured book, and two accounts are in liquidation. SARFAESI enforcement
   timelines at scale have not been demonstrated.
10. **Disclosure gaps to press for next quarter:** GNPA, credit cost/provisions, ECL staging, opex in rupees,
    borrowing mix and tenure, digital-book performance separately, CCD conversion terms, promoter holding.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
- **Openness:** management framed the call as a deliberate change of posture — *"For a long time, we have been
  focused on building the business quietly… This call marks the beginning of a more open dialogue with the
  capital market community, and we intend to build that engagement consistently from here on."*
- **Willing to take a hostile follow-up.** On the NPA jump the analyst pressed twice (*"it was 0.3 and from 0.3 it
  has jumped to 0.7, more than a 50% jump"*) and the CFO answered directly and named the cause rather than
  deflecting: *"Absolutely. I understand. Yes."*
- **Refused to over-commit once.** On an 8% cost of funds: *"8% while I may not want to comment right now."*
  That is the only visible instance of restraint; elsewhere the tone is confidently quantitative.
- **Strategy is coherent and repeatedly self-consistent** on the one thing that matters — the secured pivot: JLG
  stopped in November, unsecured run down ₹104cr → ₹60cr, secured 18% → 61%, target 75–80%.
- **Presentation quality is weak.** Materially different values for the same metric within one hour (§10.1),
  imprecise phrasing throughout (*"robustic"*, *"my raw material is money"*, *"golden AUM number"*), and the
  bookended NIM/yield figures that no one reconciled. The MD delivered the opening and the closing; **the CFO
  answered every single analyst question**, including the strategy ones directed at differentiation.
- **Analyst set is small and retail-weighted**: Sagun Capital, Bank of America Securities (dropped off the line
  before asking), an individual investor, Manthan Capital, Sapphire Capital, MoneyWisers — consistent with a
  first-ever call at this market cap.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The PPI licence is being pursued as a credit-underwriting asset, not a payments business.** The stated payoff
  is bank-statement visibility, behavioural monitoring, and in-house lead generation off the merchant/supplier
  graph — *"This gives me access towards their bank statements and also gives me to read through how the behavior
  of a customer is."* Read Regency's PPI application as an **alternative-data play**, not fee income.
- **The JLG exit was decided in a September board/management meet and executed the following month** — *"this
  second financial year onwards, so the half year onwards after the September meet, we decided that we are not
  going further of disbursing anything into JLG department."* That dates the strategic break precisely, and it
  precedes the maiden call by ~8 months.
- **Management intends to give the cost-of-funds gain away**, not bank it: *"The 2% arbitrage that I have, I want
  to pass on to the customer."* Anyone modelling falling cost of funds straight into NIM expansion is modelling
  something management explicitly said it will not do (see also §3: NIM guidance is *maintain*, not expand).
- **Reported FY26 PAT of ₹13.4cr on total income of ₹40.1cr is a ~33% net margin** (ratio computed here from the
  two management-stated figures, **not** quoted on the call) — unusually high for an NBFC borrowing at 13–14%
  with no disclosed credit cost. This is the number to interrogate first against the audited accounts.
- **A "12-month" tenure bucket is kept alive purely for treasury reasons**, not demand: *"to keep the maintain the
  healthiness of the book, we keep doing some part of a disbursement over there just to maintain the cash flows
  and collection efficiencies."* The unsecured run-down will therefore not go to zero the way JLG will.
- **Deliberate industry exclusions worth noting for read-through**: *"We are not doing any lending to any trading
  company, no real estate, no trading"*, and no land/industrial-land/agri-land collateral — a tighter screen than
  most tier-2 LAP lenders run.
- **Branch capacity vs. the AUM target is the arithmetic no one on the call tested**: ₹2–2.5cr/month across
  23 branches, against a plan to roughly double AUM to ₹500–550cr in FY27 while branches only reach ~50 by
  FY27-end. The gap is implicitly funded by ticket size and secured tenure, but it was never asked.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
No subsidiaries were named. Product-level detail given:

- **MSME secured (the core, ~61% of AUM and heading to 75–80%).** Collateral is *"a residential or commercial
  property… We do not take anything which is a land or industrial land, or no agri land, nothing. It is just a
  constructed property."* LTV *"between 50% to 60% of a collateral value"*; on a ₹30–40 lakh tier-2 ticket
  *"my collateral security value will be anything from a INR65 lakhs to INR75 lakhs kind of a range."* Residential
  collateral is incentivised: *"We lower their interest rate and reduce the PF if we get a residential property."*
  Tenure *"between four to five years… We are not going beyond 60 months at all."* ROI *"a reducing ROI from a
  20% to 24%."* Borrower profile: *"a hardware guy… somebody who's running a smaller restaurant, he's running a
  smaller 10 rooms hotel… smaller manufacturing of water bottles… manufacturing of juice, small units of…
  shampoo sachets in tier-two cities."* Explicit exclusions: *"We are not doing any lending to any trading
  company, no real estate, no trading."*
- **MSME unsecured (in run-down).** *"We were earlier having some portion of book in unsecured, which we are
  running down. So it was an INR104 crores book, today we run down that to INR60 crores."* The residual 12-month
  bucket is kept deliberately: *"we keep doing some part of a disbursement over there just to maintain the cash
  flows and collection efficiencies."*
- **Digital personal loans — "Cash My Salary" app (target 15–20% of book).** Salaried-only, *"It has to be a
  salaried guy with more than INR45,000 as a salary."* AI-based verification: *"The verification of that is
  through an AI application, which help us to take out their bank statement to review their salaries."* Approval
  *"within say about half an hour to 45 minutes."* Employer verification by official email OTP: *"a borrower has
  to put his official email ID, okay. OTP will go to his official email ID which will verify."* Economics:
  *"about close to 24% flat interest borrowing… and that's a shorter tenure of six months."* Status: past pilot —
  *"we have already run through this pilot and we see quite a good recovery."*
- **JLG microfinance (terminal run-off).** *"10.5% is my JLG book that consists today from a total AUM of
  INR261 crores. From November month onwards, we have stopped disbursing… we're discontinuing completely JLG.
  Absolutely. We have not done a single penny disbursement from the month of November onwards… There is only
  collection happening right now."*
- **Network / people.** *"we have built a presence across 23 branches with a customer base of over approximately
  16,000 plus borrower"*; *"our employee base has scaled up meaningfully… with additions across sales, credit,
  and operation functions."*
- **Geography.** *"presently concentrated in North India, particularly in the regions such as Punjab, NCR,
  Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh."* Next: *"from North India, we would like to expand to the West of India"* and
  *"a good belt of UP and MP towards eastern part"*; explicitly **not** south — *"We are not going to the South
  so soon. Maybe down the line two-three years."*
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
Management was asked the differentiation question directly (*"what differentiate your -- our company from other
player in the market?"*). What they evidenced, as opposed to asserted:
- **Local density in a 400km radius from home base.** *"In region of Punjab, Haryana, and Uttarakhand, this is our
  hometown. We are just let's say 400 kilometer within our radius to reach anywhere… we both promoters come from
  our North India background… There are regions which are negative for our NBFC as well, okay. So, we are not
  going and focusing on those cities."* The negative-geography screen is a concrete, non-generic claim.
- **Zero-DSA, 100% in-house origination.** *"We have not empanelled a single DSA till date today… It is the sales
  guy in-house team who has to go, get out and go out in the market and acquire a customer."* Real switching-cost
  economics (no commission leakage, own credit view), at the cost of scalability — which management concedes:
  *"Until recently, the business was largely branch-led and people-intensive, which gave strong control but also
  limited scalability."*
- **A hard ALM rule, stated as policy.** *"we don't want to do a transaction more than 5 years… We are strictly
  going to follow this rule of not going beyond 60 months. This not only help us to reduce the ALM mismatch, but
  also help us to reduce the risk on the longer tenure side"* — contrasted explicitly with *"other NBFCs which
  are acquiring customer for 15 years, have money for 4 years and 5 years."*
- **Tier-2 social-collateral effect** (their own framing of why recovery works): *"there is a social impact
  pressure on a borrower because you are staying in the belt… A tier-one guy's least bothered. He said, okay, I
  have defaulted INR5 crores doesn't matter… Versus a tier-two borrower, he thinks that okay, if I lose my assets…
  I lose my social impact within the vicinity."*
- **Not yet a moat:** the technology/AI claim. Management's own benchmark was *"Whether you talk about L&T
  Finance, you talk about today any of these lenders… You see their AI technology whether it is Bajaj"* — i.e.
  they are describing catch-up to incumbents, and the differentiating asset (PPI licence) is **not yet approved**.

latest_quarter.body:
- **Spread architecture as management describes it:** *"if today my borrower is giving me 20% ROI, I am borrowing
  at 12 or 13, and I having a 2% or 2.5% of opex, I am still making my spread of 3, 3 and a quarter."*
- **Target architecture:** *"we should be able to borrow our net cost of funds anything between 10.5 to 10.25…
  our opex will be between 2 to 2.5. So we have a net spread to be maintained and we can lend at 15%-16%."*
  Note this is a **lower lending rate**, deliberately — the cost-of-funds gain is to be passed through (§3).
- **Reported FY26 spread 7.1%, yield ~15%, NIM 10.75–11%.** ⚠️ The ~15% portfolio yield does not reconcile with
  20–24% MSME ROIs and ~24% flat digital ROIs; neither the analysts nor management addressed the gap.
- **Mix effect on NIM is negative-by-design** (secured MSME at a reducing 20–24% replacing unsecured/JLG), and
  management's answer to protecting NIM is the **digital barbell**: *"We have given the mix of basket of product
  will be one is our my digital lending platform which generates about close to 24% of an ROI over there, and I
  have a reducing ROI in my MSME segment… So I have further a head on my NIM."*
- **Collections cost avoided by design:** *"What happens in a MSME secured loan, right? People appoint their
  collection agencies or hire collection teams separately to collect EMIs"* — Regency instead runs NACH plus a
  future QR/PPI rail, and *"collection will happen at the branch level, the sales guy himself is responsible for
  the collection."*
- **Legal cost split:** *"we have in-house lawyers as well, plus we have outsourced lawyers as well… legal
  technical evaluation is done through a third party… legal notices of non-repayment… through our in-house
  lawyers team, and… for recovery, we are using our third-party agencies."*
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (this, and the FIRST note for this company):** Maiden earnings call. FY26 AUM ₹261.2cr (+45%), total
  income ₹40.1cr (+85%), PAT ₹13.4cr (+170%); Q4 total income ₹12cr (+43%), Q4 PAT ₹3.5cr (+37%). Secured mix
  18% → ~61% of AUM; JLG disbursement stopped Nov-2025, now 10.5% of AUM in run-off; unsecured run down
  ₹104cr → ₹60cr. Net NPA worsened 0.31% → 0.74%, attributed to the Punjab/Haryana *Karja Mukti Abhiyan* and the
  legacy JLG book. Net worth ₹106cr, CRAR 57.6%. ₹25cr CCD raised April 2026 (post balance-sheet date). RBI
  **NOC** received for a PPI licence; RedPay wallet planned within 12 months. FY27 guide: AUM ₹500–550cr,
  ₹400–450cr of new borrowings, cost of funds 11–12% within 12 months, ~50 branches, NIM held at ~10.75–11%.
  **⚠️ Multiple internal numeric contradictions within the call — see §2 and §10.1.**
- **Q1 FY27 → check:** (a) **was the PPI licence actually approved?** (guided "coming quarter" from May-2026 —
  window has lapsed); (b) audited FY26 figures vs the ones stated here, especially disbursement (₹142cr or
  ₹147cr?), net NPA and portfolio yield; (c) how much of the ₹400–450cr lender pipeline has been drawn, and
  **is any PSU bank on the list yet**; (d) realised cost of funds vs the 11–12% path; (e) branch count vs the
  23 → ~50 build; (f) JLG book vs the 70%-rundown milestone; (g) digital-book size and its own DPD, disclosed
  separately; (h) CCD conversion terms and resulting dilution; (i) whether GNPA / credit cost / opex in rupees
  are disclosed at all.

outlook.body:
- **AUM:** *"this year if we are project projecting to projections about let's to reach about INR500 crores of an
  AUM or INR550 crores when we double the numbers from here"* → **₹500–550cr FY27** (roughly a doubling of ₹261cr).
- **Long-term AUM:** *"by FY '30 we should touch our INR3000 crores of golden AUM number."*
- **Product mix:** *"80% of my lending will be in MSME secured percent. Between 15% to 20% will be my digital
  lending"*; restated as *"If we maintain our 75% to 80% book in my secured lending"* and confirmed sustainable:
  *"Absolutely sustainable."* Within the ₹500–550cr target: *"I'm talking about INR400 crores of lending in my
  MSME secured book, about close to INR75 to INR80 crores or INR100 crores lending in my unsecured book which is
  basically my digital lending platform."*
- **Borrowing / liability plan:** *"we see a strong pipeline for this year where we are raising money through
  lenders about close to INR400 to INR450 crores"* — the single most load-bearing FY27 assumption on the call.
- **Cost of funds:** *"our current cost of fund is right now about close to 13% to 14%… We want to take down so
  between 11% to 12%"*, and *"once we have public sector banks also onboarded, we should get an access of a 10%
  kind of an ROI as well."* Timeline when pressed: ***"Not more than 12 months. Not more than 12 months."***
  On 8%: *"8% while I may not want to comment right now, but Yes, we will have significant reduce on the cost of funds."*
- **NIM:** *"I keep maintaining my NIM at the level that we are today. I would not say that we'll enhance this to
  further limit but we'll be able to maintain"* — i.e. **hold ~10.75–11%**, not expand.
- **Opex:** *"my opex cost would be going forward at around 2.5 to 2.75"*; later restated *"going forward our opex
  will be between 2 to 2.5."* **⚠️ Two different guided ranges in one call.**
- **Branches:** *"Have a branch spread of about close to 50 branches by the year-end financial year end next year
  and mid of calendar year next year. So, we will double our branch numbers"* — from 23 today.
- **JLG run-off:** *"by end of the coming financial year, we should have around 70% of the book rundown. By end of
  the next calendar year, the 100% JLG book would be zero."*
- **Lending rate pass-through:** *"The 2% arbitrage that I have, I want to pass on to the customer"* — margin is
  explicitly intended to be given away to buy better-quality borrowers, not banked.
- **PPI licence:** *"in the coming financial year itself or in the coming quarter we should get the approval for
  our PPI license"* (NOC already received) — see §8/§10 on the lapsed window.
- **RedPay wallet:** *"Over the next 12 months, we plan to launch a digital wallet, named RedPay."*

outlook.body:
Not applicable in the order-book sense (a lender). The equivalents disclosed:
- **Branch disbursal capacity:** *"Today our branches have the capacity to disburse on an average per month basis
  about close to INR2 to INR2.5 crores"* — on 23 branches. Management did not reconcile this capacity against
  the ₹500–550cr AUM target on the call.
- **Average AUM per branch:** *"anything between INR10 to INR12 crores"*, location-dependent; worked examples
  *"My Varanasi has an AUM of INR10 crores. My Gopiganj has an AUM of INR3 crores. It's just 40 kilometers away."*
- **Funding pipeline (the real "order book"):** ₹400–450cr of lender lines targeted for the year, with *"further
  more to get onboarded in this coming quarter."*
- **Named existing lenders (9-plus, per the analyst's question):** *"we have ICICI Bank, we have Axis Bank, we
  have Yes Bank, we have LC Venture Debt that has given us money. We have Lighthouse Canton which has helped us
  to raise NCDs where NCD raised through Grip, we have NCDs raised through InCred Wealth, and few initial
  individuals as well. Then we have Usha Finance, we have RAR we have UC Finance."* **No public-sector bank is on
  the list yet** — which is exactly the stated route to a 10% cost of funds.
- **Sourcing:** *"we are sourcing 100% leads from our in-house. We don't have a DSA model. We have not empanelled
  a single DSA till date today."*
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **PPI licence → payments-linked collections.** *"we have also received NOC from RBI for the PPI license."* The
  intended use is not fee income but **collection and data**: *"allowing our customers once we have our PPI
  license in place to use our QR code to make payments, just like payment wallets you see what Google Pay and
  PhonePe is doing today. This gives me access towards their bank statements and also gives me to read through
  how the behavior of a customer is."*
- **RedPay wallet** (12-month horizon) — *"will enable smoother disbursement, repayments, and customer
  transactions within our ecosystem… will also give us better visibility into customer cash flows and behavior."*
- **In-house lead generation off the PPI data layer.** *"Once AI is we are enabled to get the PPI license, my AI
  will give access to all his suppliers, all his customer base, so the database itself will generate lot of leads
  in-house."* (This is a stated intent; no unit economics were attached to it.)
- **Digital MSME lending** — *"we are investing our money in technology to make sure my MSME lending also reach
  to a digital lending platform sooner or later."*
- **Cost-of-funds unlock via PSU banks** — the largest single P&L option available, and entirely unbuilt today
  (no PSU bank on the lender list).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis:
A ₹261cr-AUM Punjab-based NBFC held its **first-ever earnings call** to re-introduce itself as a secured-MSME
lender rather than the microfinance/unsecured book it used to be — and the mix shift is genuinely large and
fast: secured went from **18% → ~61% of AUM** and from **23% → ~57% of disbursement** in one year, with JLG
disbursement stopped outright in November. Reported growth is spectacular off a tiny base (AUM +45%, total
income +85%, PAT +170% to ₹13.4cr) and the balance sheet is barely levered (net worth ₹106cr, CRAR **57.6%**),
so the equity story is that ₹400–450cr of borrowing capacity, not capital, is the constraint on doubling AUM
to ₹500–550cr this year. The caution is that this is an unaudited-by-us maiden call whose **own numbers do not
reconcile with each other** (disbursement ₹142cr vs ₹147cr; portfolio yield "approximately 15%" against stated
lending ROIs of 20–24%; cost of funds quoted as 13–14%, 12–13% and "10.5 to 10.25" in the same session) — see §2
and §10, which is a materially different risk profile from a well-covered NBFC.
